utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. We are still continuing with the cross-examination of the witness. Kindly call the witness. (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Please inform the witness he is still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I want to remind you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms McMurrey. You are free now. You can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Dobodan, Mr Gotovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (In interpretation) Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Or is it "Dobonutra"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I want to go back. We were continuing our cross-examination yesterday and I asked you a lot of questions, but there are some things that I want to go back to clarify. You stated that your profession was a locksmith; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: A locksmith in your country is not someone who makes keys and sets locks, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me explain to you. I was involved in maintenance of all the fixtures and furnishings.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes. So from our standpoint a locksmith would be like a machine repairman, would he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was mostly involved with tools and storage area.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And when you say tools, you used heavy machinery; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: When you say tools, what kind of machinery did you use?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not use any machines. I was a locksmith. That is a metal worker. I was involved in maintaining tools and sometimes I would be bringing tools in and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am just trying to figure out what kind of tools. When you say you are a metal worker, did you work with some kind of metal-making machine of some sort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I mostly worked in the warehouse. I was issuing tools and I was taking tools to the maintenance and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. I think I understand your position now. Thank you very much. I want to go -- I would like to go back now to building number 22 that we discussed yesterday and, just for clarification purposes, you were in building number 2 from May 23rd until about June 13th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, approximately. I did not count the days. I did not know the exact dates.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: At the time that you were in building number 22, the first time, it was not an infirmary or a hospital. It was just a holding facility; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was a storage area for fire-fighting equipment. There were hoses there and a pump.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: For the purposes of the people in number 22, they were not being treated for injuries then; they were being held at that point, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were detained there. They were under arrest, whichever way you want to put it.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Then some time in the middle of June you had an interview with some people, and then you were moved to hangar number 6; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who I talked to, but I was transferred to hangar number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Then from the middle of June until some time in the early part of July you were in hangar number 6; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Then some time early in July you were transferred back to building number 22 until August 30th, and you remained there during that period of time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I remained there until 30th August.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Then during the time you were in building number 22, the second time, it was being utilised as a medical facility or an infirmary of some sort, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were 12 beds there and 12 patients, and there were two doctors, who were also prisoners, who worked there, a male nurse and so on. The male nurse was also a prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You just told us today for the first time that there were 12 beds inside the infirmary; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I told you that before.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In building number 22 you could not see from building number 22 to tunnel Number 9, could you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And, in fact, tunnel Number 9 was at least 60 metres away from building number 22, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, when you were moved to hangar number 6, I would like to ask you to -- can you draw? -- If I were to give you a piece of paper, can you draw the seating arrangement as you remember it of the prisoners inside hangar number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was a circle or row all around the room and there were two rows down the middle of the room, and of course we sat on the concrete.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You were seated in one of the rows down the middle of the hangar number 6, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the middle, in one of the rows in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You were seated actually on the -- from hangar number 6, as you walk in through the door, there is a row in the middle directly to the left and then there would be called the second row in the middle, would there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two rows.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And you were seated for basically almost a month on the second row in the middle, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I guess it was the second row. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: It was the row closest to the back of hangar number 6, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It wasn't very far from the door.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But it was the one closest to the back. It was not the row closest to the door, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was in one of the rows that were in the middle of the room. I was very close to the exit door.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So it's your testimony to this court today that you were not in the second half of the row towards the back. Is that what you are saying today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't really describe now which row is the first one and which is the second one. I can only tell you that I sat in one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: If I gave you have a clean piece of paper right now, could you draw a photograph -- I mean a drawing and illustrate where you were sitting in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't really draw. I think it is not really difficult to explain if you look from above towards the door, I sat in the middle row to the left, if you look down the hangar towards the exit door.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just offer him a piece of paper and see if he can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: He has told you he cannot. Why are you offering him? He has told you a few seconds ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am just trying to clarify for the court where he was sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: He just stated that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I believe if he illustrated where he was sitting he would not be close to the door. He has said he was close to the door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: It is easy to explain. That is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Are you clear from his explanation, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You are asking the questions. It is for you to get out of the questions what you want.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I just want it to be clear for the court. That is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: It is your case. We will know how to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you about hangar number 6. You claimed it was 200 x 40 metres; is that correct? I am sorry. Did you say it was 200 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall really. I don't know if this is the size. Do you mean the length of the hangar? I don't know if it was 240 metres long.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I think the dimensions you quoted were 200 x 40, so it would be 200 metres long and 40 metres wide. Is that about what you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was my assessment. It may have been smaller than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: 200 metres long?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: That is very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is more than a furlong.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, I know it is very long. I think it is probably longer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was very long.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I believe that is what the witness had stated before. That is why I was trying to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I can understand 200 feet, but 200 metres long ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Metres? More than 600 feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You can have 1,000 persons in 200 metres long.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Is that like a football field? I am sorry. I am really not familiar with metres myself, so it is difficult for me to visualise. I think the way he stated it was much larger than it was actually. I was just trying to clarify his perception of the building itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: 110 yards would make 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was longer than it was wide. That is for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. I think the court is aware of the approximate size of the building itself, but I also want to clarify: while you were sitting in there for almost a month, there are no windows that anybody can look out of that hangar, are there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were windows, but they were placed very high and they were closed.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And the windows are up near where the ceiling meets the walls at about 3 metres up; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ceiling was arched and the height from the concrete floor up to the windows was about 3 metres. We didn't measure it. We had to look straight ahead of us. We could not look around.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Havala.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: There was only one door that was used while you were there. It was a small door to the right as you faced hangar number 6; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was one door.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: At night you had a toilet can inside the hangar that you all used to relieve yourself that was taken out and cleaned during the day, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was right next to the door.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: The doors -- there were some sliding doors in the front of the hangar that were never opened; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about those doors. I haven't seen them.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, the wall that faced the front of hangar number 6, what I would like for you to show the court is that there were no holes in that wall through which you could look out, were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And although you were sitting in the middle of the building, around the bottom of the building from the inside it was sealed from the wall to the floor, was it not? You were not able to reach your hands out of the building, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, we were not able to.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And whenever you had to go to the toilet, they provided toilets for you toward the back of the hangar number 6, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of the hangar on the canal, on the ditch. That was for urination. We would go there in groups of five to six and later on fifteen, ten.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, you participated in digging a trench that was used as a toilet facility, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Are you telling the court you did not dig a trench?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You also stated that the food was little and you were just served stale bread; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand the word that was used in the translation. Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: That you had very little food and what you were served was very old, hard bread; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just hold on for a minute. I do not think we have got his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We used the word that means "stale". Yes, it was very old.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I don't think the answer that has come on the transcript is clear. You said: "Are you telling the court that you did not help in digging the trench?" He says: "No". He really means: "Yes, I did not". Here it would be: "I was not telling this court". So the transcript is not correct. I think the idiom in English is slightly different. When you say in the positive you say: "Yes, I did". You do not say: "No" as an answer to a negative question. The idiom in English is slightly different. Probably the evidence in a different language is coming out, so the transcript is not truly representing the answer which is given.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. I can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us go back a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. I will ask him the same question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: There were two questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, you stated to this court that you did not dig a trench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: No. The first question: "You did not participate in digging a trench?"

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am not reading it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: When he said: "No", then you asked whether he did not dig this trench. That was the sequence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Yes. He said: "Yes, I did not tell the court", not "no".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not dig.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Those were the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is not the full answer. The transcript does not represent truly what he said because of the difference in the idiom in the English language. He should give the answer in the positive: "Yes, I did it", no matter what the form of the question is. When he wants: "No, I did not", the answer will be clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now is the record clear?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I think so. Some of the answers are coming in that form. So I just wanted to warn you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I appreciate it. If I am asking the question in the wrong form, please let me know, because of course I do not speak Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You are not asking questions in the wrong form. It is a translation in a different language, the idiom being different.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Just let me know if I need to go back. I will be happy to, but the statement was that Mr Gotovac did not participate in digging a trench. Okay. Now you said that there was very little food and the food that was served to you was hard, old bread; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was stale. The bread was stale.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You also claimed while you were in the medical facility that the facilities were terrible. You did not have medicine, you did not have enough water and you did not have enough food; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I do not know what kind of infirmary you are referring to, when this was just a storage facility for fire-fighting equipment. There can't be any facilities for providing medical treatment there.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, we all know when you were in building 22 from 15th July to August 30th, it was being used to treat ill people, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to show you a videotape, and I would like for you to identify some of these people on the videotape for me, if you do not mind. I am going to ask the Video Department to play the videotape now. Your Honours, I would like to say that this is a videotape that we got from the prosecution, so they are aware of it. It was seized by the prosecution from Mr Delalic. So I would like to run this small -- it is only about one minute -- videotape, if you do not mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not -- I am sure that Ms McMurrey is correct, but just for the record, I believe that it should be reflected what video this is, so it can be admitted into evidence. When I talked with Ms McMurrey earlier this morning, and I have not seen the video, she said she did not know. I saw that it says "I46" on the video. So at least for the record -- which is, I believe a numbering system -- so at least now for the record I would like it to reflect that the video is I46.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am sure what Ms McHenry says is accurate; I do not know. This was made off one of the 90 tapes seized from Mr Delalic. At this point I do not know which one it was. I did not make the tape, so ... but it is from the prosecution's tapes. I will be happy to provide the exact tape some time in the future for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You mean you are introducing evidence you have no idea about?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Right now I am just playing it for impeachment purposes. I know it was seized from Mr Delalic. The prosecutor gave it to us. We will be happy to introduce it into evidence if there is no objection from the prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I am only worried about your claim that you do not know anything about the evidence you are trying to introduce.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I know something about it. I know it was made in August. I know it is a journalist from Sarajevo who went to Celebici and is interviewing the prisoners from Celebici. I can authenticate that point. As from which tape it came off of, I am not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is I46, as Ms McHenry says.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I accept that. Can we play the videotape now? (Videotape played).

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I will come back and freeze it and as we go, Mr Gotovac, please, I would like you to identify these people and tell me if you are in this video: okay? Could we stop the tape for a second. I would like to go back to the beginning. Could the interpretation interpret for the court what the question and answer is on the videotape and also, from the first part -- the first part, Mr Gotovac, that is the inside of building number 22, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stravko Cecez was in number 6. This is not a tape made in 22.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: This is not the inside of building number 22 with the beds and the patients right in front of you? Can we put the videotape back on the screen, please, so he can see that? That gentleman, do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. You are saying that these are not the beds and this is not the inside of building number 22, where you spent a month and a half; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is not very clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: We are going to play it again right now and I am going to ask the interpreters to please, if you can, interpret what is being said in this interview, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just like to clarify for what purpose is this tape being used and for what purpose is it being interpreted? In particular we do not object to the admission of the evidence, but I do not see anything that is going to impeach, and then if we are going to be asking him about what other people said in an interview, when he is not the person being interviewed, I fail to see how the defence counsel can use it for impeachment at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I will be happy to respond. When you see the tape, in a moment the tape shows the medical facility. One of the doctors who is a prisoner here is telling how most of these people were injured from the shelling in Konjic. He says he was in here during this period of time the tape was made in August. He should be able to identify these people, number one, and secondly, the second part of the interview is some other Serbian prisoners telling about how much food they have. They have so much extra food that they are giving it to some of the people outside in the village. It is the doctors, an interview with the doctors, telling about how the people are treated and how it is reacting. He said the conditions were terrible, they did not have enough food, they did not have enough water. He knows these people in this tape, and I am going to ask him are they telling the truth or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Please, were any of those people in the same facility with him at the same time?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: They are coming forward to testify?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I do not know if they are coming to forward to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not know how you will impeach what he said happened to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: No, your Honour, we are talking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Why do you not listen to me? I listened to you. He said the food was not good enough. You are now bringing a tape to show that there are people who said they had surplus food and they were giving it to people in the village. Is that not what you have just said?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it shows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: In contradiction to what he has said?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Then these are not people who are likely to have been in the same place with him at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, this is exactly the summer, the period of 1992 where he says there was not enough food, and the medical facilities were bad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: When he was there?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: When he was there. This is exactly the same time. This is August of 1992. It is exactly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Your reasoning might be a good one, but these people should be inmates with him for you to be able to impeach him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: They are inmates with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is what she is asking him, to identify them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I was going to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If they are inmates with him, then you might be right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I believe but I am not sure -- I think Mr Gotovac can identify himself on this video, your Honour, if you just give me an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Nobody disturbed you. You have been through it once.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, but now we need to hear the interpretation of what's being said and give him an opportunity to identify the people he recognises on the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Including himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Including himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let him identify himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I would love to. Thank you. Okay. Mr Gotovac, this gentleman that you see right in front of you, who is that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He says he does not know. The picture is not clear. Move to the next frame.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Let us go ahead and play the whole tape through right now and let the interpreters interpret what the prisoners are saying. Then I will have him identify each one, if you do not mind. I think that is the easiest way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: There are so many questions. Who is interviewing them; what is happening; if he was also there. These are the things.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I believe it will show he was also there, your Honour. Let us hear the whole thing first and then I will take it apart. Okay. Thank you. May we have the interpretation of what is being said?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is a visit by the International Red Cross about the conditions and the rights of the prisoners and the visits of their next of kin. Their food is better even than what our fighters have. I had a restaurant in Bradina. I am a war prisoner here. How are they treating you? Fairly correctly. The food is good, three times a day. Cecez Stravko from Donje Selo. I came on May 20 ... As he said, they have given us food three times a day. It is not so bad. The extra food we give to the elderly, because they can eat more. There is order and peace in here. We are in the compound in the Celebici prison and this is Petko Grubac in the infirmary. In the beginning we were the prisoners and we worked here as doctors. Now we have been released and now we come here and work during the day. How were the prisoners injured? Practically they are in relatively good shape. Practically that means that it is satisfactory. They were injured during the combat operations and in the sports hall in Konjic. We have six of them there. Two are pretty good. The other three are much better than... We have brought them here to be treated and I think that within a week or two they will be all right."

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry. This is not a complete interpretation. It is very hard to hear portions of it. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I apologise to the interpretation department for not getting this to you ahead of time. It is my fault and I accept full responsibility but thank you for trying so hard to interpret that. I believe that the court could kind of understand what was being said, and if you do not mind, I will question Mr Gotovac from what we have just seen. I also want to ask Mr Gotovac: do you need glasses to be able to see the screen or can you see it? Okay. I do not know if you saw it the first two times it has been played, but -- can we have the videotape back up, just a couple of frames at a time, if that is possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was able to recognise Ratko Cecez, but what he is saying is not correct. It was under duress. He is saying that there was so much food almost to be thrown away. That was not true.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, I would like to ask you some questions and then I would like for you to answer me, if that would be possible. First of all: you were present when this tape was made, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, the journalist that is speaking in here is a woman named Jodranka Milosevic, who was a Serbian journalist from Sarajevo; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see her there and I don't know her.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So are you stating to this court that you are not on this videotape?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has already said that he does not know. Certainly I saw it and I could not tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has not said he does not know. Just one frame was shown to him and he said the picture is not clear. He has not said yet: "I am not among them".

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I thought he said: "I did not remember that I was here."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He can see himself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Could we take the next couple of frames on this? He said he did not identify this gentleman but can we take the next one? Do you know this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You do not know him? Okay. Can we move to the next one, please? Now, Mr Gotovac, who is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You do not know that gentleman either? Okay. Can we go to the next one, please? Do you know this gentleman? Mr Gotovac, do you need to put your glasses on to see the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Can we take the next one, please? Now see the gentleman over there on the last bed, do you know who that man is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The white shirt?

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I just can't make him out.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, could you please leave your glasses on, because this is a continuing questioning from the video, and I need for you to be able to see. Now can we go to the next people in number 22? Do you see this person who looks like he is fairly ill and he cannot sit up? Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see the image, but I can't make out who it is.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go on to the next few frames then please? Do you know who this is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know that anyone was sitting in a bed in the undershirt, because we weren't able to undress like that.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So you are saying you do not know who this man is; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. See, this one took his shirt off. We could not do that. I can't accept that.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am not asking about his clothing. I am asking: do you identify the man? Do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. As I said, this gentleman took off his shirt, and we were not allowed that, so I don't know who that is.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go to the next ones then, please? Now, Mr Gotovac, do you know who this person is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that man there.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go to the next portion of the video, please? Those are the medical supplies that were held in 22, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a door -- there was a table next to the door, but I can't see the door from here.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, but the table contained medical supplies, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I see things on the table, but there is no-one around the table, nobody that I know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let us go on to the rest of the video. Who is this person right here? You can identify him, can you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He looks like Relja, but I don't know if it's Relja.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Relja was one of the doctors that was treating you there for a month and a half?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a doctor. Yes, but he looks a bit different here. It looks like Relja, but I am still not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go on a little further, please? The doctor -- I mean, the person standing next to him, that is another doctor from the facility, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Petko Grubac.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Petko Grubac treated you, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Can we move a little further on the video, please? Let me stop. You have seen this woman before, have you not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: There is no woman there. There is no woman on the TV.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: The interviewer right on the left-hand side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: You have never seen Jodranka Milosevic before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have never seen her.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You have never seen her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Let us move on a little bit further on the videotape. You have identified this man as Petko Grubac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Petko Grubac, but he was not this fat. He was much thinner. He has -- this is very large. He was a short man, and he looks bigger here, but yes, this is Petko Grubac. I recognise him now by his hair but I don't know the journalist. I never saw her.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Havala. Can we move to the next part of the screen, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Now you know who this man is, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Radko Cecez, but he spoke very incorrectly.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And he was a prisoner along with you when you were in hangar number 6, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He is the one who was distributing the slices of bread, and he had an assistant. I don't know who that was, but this man is not alive. He died.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But he looks pretty healthy in August of 1992, does he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what the state of his health was there.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Let us move on in the video, please. Okay. Who is this gentleman right here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You do not know this man at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't. It doesn't look like anybody I know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So you do not know a man named Djordjo Morcajic, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard of him but he's a younger man, so I never had any contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But he was also --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: He was also a prisoner in hangar number 6 at the same time you were, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not there with us. I never saw him in any of the beds.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am sorry. He was in hangar number 6 with you, was he not, not in number 22?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then it was your mistake, not mine. Number 6, but again a younger man, so I wouldn't have known him. Maybe he was from Bradina, but I didn't know many of those people up there. Some of the older ones, yes, but not the younger ones.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, Mr Gotovac, you know you are under oath right now. Are you telling the court you have never seen this man before in hangar number 6?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to object. He has already said he does not know -- there were younger men in hangar number 6 and he does not know who all of them are. I must object to this -- what I can only call badgering of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I asked him if he knew him but he said he did not know him. I am asking him if he has seen him. He does not have to know him. I want him to tell this court he has never seen him in hangar number 6; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible that he was in number 6 or maybe even in Number 9, but there were a lot of people there. There was a mass of people. Sometimes I would not even see my own neighbour well. We weren't allowed to look around. We had to look in front of ourselves, and there was not enough light.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Could we move on to the next frame, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think there should be an end to this television trial.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us know exactly what you are asking. We cannot go like this endless.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I want to go back to building number 22 where he is in the photograph and I want him to identify himself. It is coming up to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Is that still on this same tape?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, I believe. Is it not? Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If that is exhausted, then I do not think we should go further, but you started with an impeachment. Except you are still continuing on the impeachment ... In formulating the impeachment, let us know where we are.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I am asking you what you want to impeach so we know the extent of your cross-examination. You cannot be going this wild not knowing exactly what you are doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I know what I am doing, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I would be happy to explain it, if you would let me. He has said he was in building number 22 from the 1st July until August 30th. So far he has not identified anybody else that was in there during that time. Now there is going to be a photograph of him in that building, and if he was in that building and he cannot identify those people, then he must be not telling the truth, if he was there for a month and a half. He has also stated that they did not have food, they did not have medical facilities, and this videotape is showing he is not telling the truth about that also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: You mean because someone else in a video facility said something, he must be lying.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, I think that it is impeachment. If he was there for a month and a half in that building and he does not know the other people around him, then it shows that maybe he is not telling the whole truth here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Obviously they are only all the people around him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: These are the only people around him. There are no others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Show him his own frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let him see himself. When we find him, we will know where we are going.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Can we have the next part of the video, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Focus on the picture where he is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: You are claiming, Mr Gotovac, that you do not know this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognise both doctors, and there was also a male nurse there, Brane Gligorevic, and I never saw him. There was Kuljanin next to me. I never saw him. What Radko said about the food, I am not also saying there was no food. There was some food but there was not that much food.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to go ahead and run this. When he sees himself -- I was just informed that he was on the first part of the videotape and he did not identify himself. I believe that is when he did not have his glasses on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If anyone else can identify him, they will point it out to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Show him the frame.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: This is not you. Let us move on and see the rest of this video. Is that him?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Well, you know, it is five years ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must object. This is a very bad quality photograph. No-one, including counsel, is able to recognise anyone. He has already said he cannot recognise anyone. To continue to show him this same thing over and over again, I do not see the point.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: He is on this videotape. I have been informed by everybody here he is on this tape, if we can just continue. Please, we have just five more seconds. For the judicial economy of not having to recall him, can I just please complete this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us not use your extra vigours to include judicial economy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I explain about the glasses, please? My glasses were broken in the prison, and so this is a very different pair of glasses. I had 3.5 on one eye and 4 on the other, and what I have here is something completely different. It is 3. So the glasses that I have here are not the right ones. All this is not clear enough to me. I recognise the two doctors. The male nurse, he used to be next to the table, but I could not see him in these pictures at all, not once. I am not saying that this is not number 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Are any of your defendants able to recognise him in the video? If they do, they should point him out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Which one is him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I do not think we have come to that. I want to ask him that. Mr Delic and Mr Delalic can identify him on the video. I would also like to add if he cannot see because his glasses were broken in 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let someone else identify him in the video, and they will point that one out to him: "This is you."

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Anybody back here, when you see Mr Gotovac, would you just please holler: "Halt"? Would that work? Okay. Can you play the rest of the video, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DELIC
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: This man, who is this man, Mr Gotovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It looks like me, but it has something white on the forehead. I never had, but Nedjo Kuljanin should be next to me but I can't make him out, but it should be Nedjo Kuljanin because we lay next to one another, because he was helping me for eight days. I couldn't go out on my own. I saw that Nedjo Kuljanin was on the right and I was on the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: We need not pursue this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, you do recognise yourself in the video, though, do you not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: He did not say it was him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did recognise, but barely, and I know how I recognised myself, because of Nedjo, because he was next to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Can I just let the record reflect that it was Mr Delic that recognised Mr Gotovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: And also Mr Gotovac recognised himself. My next question, Mr Gotovac: you were there in this facility obviously during that time from 1st July until the end of August, and you do not know these other people? You cannot recognise these other people around you? Is that what you are telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not recognise this Djare. Petko and Relja, the doctors, I did recognise.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And the other patients around you in number 22, did you not recognise them?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Objection. Asked and answered several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ODIO BENITO
utterances.text: Yes. I sustain the objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am going to go on to another area, but the people that talked on this videotape, that spoke: are you telling me that they are telling an untruth about the conditions at Celebici?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Objection. Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: He said that several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I am going to go back to hangar number 6. When you were in hangar number 6 how many guards were guarding you at one time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. We had to sit down and look in front of us. When the door opened, we only had to look in front, and at night you could not see, and I never counted them.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Now you have gone into great detail earlier about someone named Esad Landzo, also known as Zenga; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And you described him as "not abnormal", did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, his behaviour was normal.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Now, you also said --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he was aware of everything he was doing. He was not unaware.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. You also said that there was an Arab or a black film crew that came to Celebici; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that last night.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I explained that, that I could not speak, that my throat hurt, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, and you also said that your two sons and a Spasoje Mil -- I am sorry. I cannot remember the other person that was with you -- Spasoje Miljevic was with you at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When they left, the camera crew, when they left, then Landzo Esad took me out. His nickname is Zenga, and he took out my two sons and Spasoje Miljevic, and, as I explained yesterday -- I do not know why I have to repeat that -- he put the gasmask on my older son and Spasoje Miljevic but not on my younger son and he asked me what I said and then he beat me. He asked them what they said and then he beat them. Since my older son started to mumble because he had enough of the gasmask, he took it off and beat him about the face, and he forced him to go inside the hangar. Then he took off Spasoje's mask and forced him back into the hangar and started to cut my younger son with a knife and forced him back into the hangar. Then my Calvary began. I had to put my hands behind my head and then he kicked me in the scrotum and on the side in my ribs. Then I tried to protect that place on my side, on my abdomen, where then I had the hernia. Then when he asked me why I was holding it, and I had explained that to him before, when he had taken me out before, and during all this horror my tongue went back inside my throat, so that I was unconscious for a time. I don't know what was happening with him during that time. Then the male nurse, who was in the prison with us, Brane Gligorevic, he came out and he had a shoehorn probably in his pocket. Then he pulled my tongue out using that shoehorn. I felt that he was regaining consciousness, but I was urinating blood.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr Gotovac. Now would you answer the one question I asked? My question was: there was a black Arab film crew that came to Celebici, was there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They had some instruments. I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I would just like to ask you, please, if you would just listen to my question and just answer the question, because I will let you explain when we get to those certain events; okay? Now, the Arab film crew asked you a question about did the Serbs not kill the Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they asked me whether they did, and I said: "I don't know." My answer was: "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And did you recognise the language that they were speaking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But you claimed they were black; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were some people there who were black. I was shaking. I was very afraid. I didn't even dare to look at them properly. I was really, really scared. I didn't know what was happening to me.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: After the film crew left, that is when you claim that Mr Landzo beat you. Is that what you are claiming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He beat me then, and he tortured me very badly, and Hazim Delic came and Brane asked -- actually he asked Brane: "Where does this blood come from?" Brane explained they broke my tooth when they were trying to pull out my tongue, but the real problem was I was urinating blood. I still have real problems with my prostrate gland. Shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: No. I would just like you to answer my question, please. We have an agreement, do we not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: This is cross-examination, you know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I would like to have a little bit of control over it myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: That is the problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, I know. Now you claimed that Mr Landzo jumped on you in a kind of Ninja-type jump; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He went behind my back. I sat down on the concrete. First, he kicked me in the scrotum. Then he went behind my back and he jumped and kicked me with his knees and with his army boot, so that my shoulder is as a result deformed, and it aches all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now your claim also is that both of your sons and Spasoje Milanjevic witnessed this. Is that your claim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Miljevic" is the name.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, and they all three saw this happen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Spasoje could not see and my younger son could not see, because they had been forced inside, and my older son appeared with Brane to save me from suffocating. Then Delic told them to put me inside his Fica car. They didn't dare to --

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I will get to that, if you just give me a chance. I would like to ask questions as we go along. You also claim that Mr Landzo has studied karate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what I heard from his peers in the prison, but I don't know that, from men his age in the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So you would not know if his brother was the one who actually studied karate, would you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, you would not know that his brother Nejad looks like Mr Landzo, would you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You wouldn't know that his brother Nejad is also known as "Zenga" either, would you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that Esad was nicknamed Zenga, and I know him very well, because he caused me a lot of harm, and he injured my human dignity, and he told me that I would be dead in eight days.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So after you claim that you were beaten by Mr Landzo, you had some kind of attack, did you not, where your tongue went back in your throat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I explained that already.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: This attack, was it diagnosed by the male nurse as a heart attack, as a seizure? Was it diagnosed as something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You were taken immediately to the medical facility, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He took me there, but it wasn't an infirmary. It was the fire-fighting storage place.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You were taken to number 22?

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And, in fact, you walked to the car, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I crawled. I couldn't walk. I crawled.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You were not carried on a stretcher, were you?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Objection. Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: He said he crawled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The car was close by and I was able to crawl there, and he opened the door and told me to crawl in, and that is what I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: When you got to building number 22, which doctor of those two that you identified examined you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He called Relja and he said: "Relja, tell me, will this guy croak?", and Relja took me in.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Did Relja give you any diagnosis about whether -- excuse me; I have not finished the question -- about whether you had some kind of stroke, or heart attack, or seizure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: I want to go back just a little bit to when the male nurse came out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think the Trial Chamber will now rise. We will come back at 11.30. (11.10 am) (Short break) (11.35 am)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly invite the witness. (Witness returned to court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Will you kindly remind him he is still on his oath?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I am reminding you that you are still under oath, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms McMurrey, do you mind if I just take a second of your time?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Of course not, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: And ask a simple question which has been worrying me. Does the witness know whether any guards stayed with them inside the hangar, whether they had guards staying with them apart from those outside?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Was any guard inside the hangar also all the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes they would be there, but for the most part they were outside behind the door. That is outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: That is enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr Gotovac, I think we had just talked about the black film crew and what was happening to you afterwards, and you had just testified that you had had some kind of seizure or something where your tongue had gone back, and then there was a male nurse who was also a prisoner, was there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And that male nurse you said came out of hangar number 6 to attend to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: When you were taken into Celebici, and all of the prisoners, all of your personal belongings were seized, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't have anything on me at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But none of the other prisoners with you were allowed to keep any of their belongings, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So you claim that this prisoner ran out of hangar number 6 to attend to you and used a shoehorn to extract your tongue; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a shoehorn which you used to help put on your shoes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now, you would not be surprised that no other witnesses can recount your beating, would you?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe this kind of questioning is objectionable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How would he know?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I had asked him if he would be surprised. That is his own perception.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Entirely irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Relevant all right, but how would he know?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Mr Gotovac, you claim at least one of your sons was present at the time you were suffering this seizure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Did he say he was suffering any seizure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the elder one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am trying to find out --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not like you introducing things that are new. He did not say he suffered a seizure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Whatever the condition is where his tongue goes down his throat, whatever that condition is, when you were suffering that, your eldest son was present; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us know what you are asking him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. Somebody from the door must have called the nurse or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Let us have your question properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Was your son present when you had your tongue go down your throat outside hangar number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was. He was standing when Delic said to take me to his Fica car. Neither Brane nor my son dared go there, so I crawled there because the car was very close. Then he told me to crawl in and I did, but I said that several times.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Is your son coming to testify?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Under what grounds?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: This witness does not know about other witnesses who may or may not be coming to testify, and, two, it is entirely irrelevant to his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it is a completely proper question, and I would like to have him answer it if his son is going to come testify about what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Do you know whether your son is coming to testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Which brings me to another line of questioning. Yesterday every time Ms McHenry would ask you a question about your seeing injuries on someone else, you testified that they would be the best person to answer that question, because they are coming to testify. Did you not say that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not what I said. They are scattered around the world and I don't know where everybody is.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But she asked you specifically -- one I remember is Nedeljko Draganic. She said: "You saw his injuries, did you not?" You said: "He would be the best one and he is coming to testify." Is that not what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nedeljko Draganic is here. He is in the witness room and he is waiting. I don't know when his turn is going to be but he is here and he is waiting.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Can I caution, please, with respect to some witnesses that are going to be protected, that she not ask this witness about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. I was not aware that that one was protected. That is the only name.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That one is not, but with respect to some others they may be.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: With my difficulty with the names I could not remember anyway except that one. You know these other people you testified about yesterday are coming to testify because they are here with you. Is that what you are testifying to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Nedeljko is here at the movement. He is back in the witness room. I don't know when his turn is going to be.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You have always talked about while you were allegedly in your encounter with Mr Landzo that something snapped in your stomach. Is that what you testified to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Inside it snapped. I think that it was this -- it is something under the skin and it is like a membrane, and so the intestines are coming out. So I have to undergo surgery for it.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now, you were released from Celebici on August 30th, 1992, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And you claim that you have been suffering from great pain from this hernia; is that what you claim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is true that I had pains and I have them today as well.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, you were released on August 30th, 1992, and you did not see a doctor until May of 1995, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shortly before, about ten, fifteen days, I was seen by doctors, but it was in August.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: You must be referring to the doctors at Celebici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in Celebici, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So since you were released, you did not see anyone until May of 1995, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not complain to the doctors any more. I just carried it. Only on one occasion I had a referral, and I went to Trebinje, but they did not perform surgery. They said that first I had to be verified as an invalid.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, yesterday, even though you claim you saw a doctor in 1995, yesterday in your testimony your exact quote was: "My stomach is protruding every year more and more. I wish that I could have it checked by somebody." That is what you said yesterday, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said and last night in the witness room they took pictures of my shoulder and my stomach and my hand, and so those people who took those pictures, they may be able to testify to that.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But you were a 60-year-old man in 1992, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 60, 61, somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Other than your testimony, we have no proof whether you suffered from that hernia before you went to Celebici or not, do we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has not used the word "hernia", has he?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: No, he does not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Then why introduce a word which he probably does not understand?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr Gotovac, do you claim to this court that you are suffering from a hernia, and I do not know if that is something that interprets into Bosnian or not. Do you understand that term?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand these conditions. I think that I would need a longer explanation to understand what they are.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Are you claiming that one of your injuries from Celebici was a tear in some of your intestines or your stomach lining that causes -- can somebody help? -- I don't know how to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I am not a doctor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: That causes an enlargement of that tissue in that area? Is that what your claim is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in the intestines. It is the lining. So the intestines moved to behind the skin.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay, but it is some kind of tear in your stomach; is that what you are claiming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Other than your testimony that something snapped at that time, we have no proof whether you were suffering from that before July of 1992 or not, do we?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was very healthy, healthy as steel.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: But the only proof we have of that is what you tell us. You do not have any medical records from before that, do you?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must object. I do not object if she asks has he any medical records, but in terms of proof, for instance, there will be other proof, for instance, from the Serbian doctors who saw him. I do not believe her characterisation or the witness' characterisation of what proof there is is proper for this court. If she wants to ask him if he has medical records he can provide, I do not object to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: May I respond, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, you have got him to answer that he was very healthy before that beating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Like steel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If you want to respond, you can do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Just for clarification, any doctor that he has seen after the fact can testify that maybe there is the existence of this condition or not, but since we have no records from before that, there is no-one saying that the condition did not exist before July of 1992. That is the only thing I was trying to show the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, he has told you what he was before then.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Right. You were a 61-year-old man of steel; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. At that time he was as strong as steel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was 60, 61, something like that. Now I am 66.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: You were retired in 19 -- in 1992, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I retired in 1990.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes. So in 1992 you were already a retired individual, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Objection. Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. He has answered that question several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. So were you retired as an invalid in 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So you had not suffered any injuries on the job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just I went prematurely into retirement and I had never gone to the doctor's while I worked.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Now I want to also -- we will request -- can we address this matter right now? We have no really concrete medical examination of Mr Gotovac, and Ms McHenry and I spoke earlier about asking the court for an independent doctor to examine him. We are both in agreement on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Frankly I do not know the type of counsel you are. You are cross-examining. It is not your case.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: No, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Go ahead with your cross-examination and finish with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I will finish and then we will address this matter? I just thought while we were talking about his injuries ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: When you deal with your ... I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, you also claim you have injury on the palm of your hand; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from the cigarette.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And you do know that Mr Landzo does not smoke cigarettes, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a cigarette in his hand at the time. I don't know if he's a smoker or not.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So he must have taken that cigarette from another guard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How would he know?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: You claim he put the cigarette out on your hand; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. You claim that that injury from putting a cigarette out on your hand has caused deformation of some tendons in your hand; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The doctors told me that some tendon gave way, that two -- and two of my fingers are still not bending properly.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You have some kind of medical proof that that injury on your hand is a burn, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here I gave it to the prosecution. There is something there.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: There is no evidence that that injury is a burn, is there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time I didn't have a picture taken of it, only a doctor looked at it and I orally confirmed it, and there were three doctors who signed it.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: And the doctors you are talking about were the Serbian doctors provided by the people from Belgrade, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That was in Visegrad. I went to the doctor there.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: They were the Serbian doctors, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For one female doctor, I know that she was Serbian, and I never asked the other two doctors what they were.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: Are they Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I thought medical practice is a matter of professional ethics, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: They are supposed to be. I am hoping those doctors will be here in order to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What are you talking about their nationalities and religion and the like. I thought it was a professional thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not know what that has to do with their professional expertise.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I think you are generalising because these refer to detention camps, and they are not unprejudiced, unbiased reports by any means. When the doctors come to testify, we will be able to show that to you then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Try and remove some of these clouds in your mind. You will see better.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: If you try and remove some of these clouds, you will see better.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: After the fourth witness -- I hope by the time this is over with, we are able to remove a lot of clouds, but it is kind of hard digging through all this at the first and we are doing the best we can. Now, I want to go to some claims that you made yesterday. You know for a fact that Mr Landzo did not kill Cedo Avramovic, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: In fact, you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he was between the two rows at dawn, and he was stripped to the waist and he died there. I don't know what happened. So when I don't know, I cannot say anything.

utterances.speaker: MS MCMURREY
utterances.text: So you are claiming you did not know that Mr Avramovic died of natural causes. Is that what you are telling this court today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
